prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the pii-chat agent (card support: identity checks, lost and stolen cards, replacements) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a carer speaking for a member. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"When a carer is speaking on a member’s behalf, I should ask whether the member is present and able to confirm permission, and if not, I must follow our third-party authority process before discussing anything account-specific."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the caller says they are a carer, I often need to slow the conversation down and separate the identity check from the reason for calling, so I do not rush into card actions before confirming authority."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the carer cannot pass security for the member, I should not rely on their explanation alone; I need to offer the correct route for the member to call, or for formal authority to be set up first."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a carer is clearly helping with day-to-day tasks, I should use plain, respectful language and avoid jargon, because it makes the security questions and next steps much easier to follow."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member has difficulty speaking, hearing, or remembering details, it is helpful to check whether the carer can support the call while I still direct the key verification questions to the member wherever possible."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the request is about a lost or stolen card, I should treat urgency separately from authority: I can help with immediate safety steps, but I still need the correct permission before ordering a replacement or discussing card details."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a carer is arranging a replacement card, I should confirm the delivery address and who will receive the post, because this avoids confusion if the member does not manage their own mail."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the carer sounds unsure about what authority they have, it is better to explain the options clearly than to keep asking the same question, as many callers do not know the difference between informal support and formal permission."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member is not available, I should check whether there is a registered third-party, power of attorney, or other approved arrangement on the record before I proceed with any card support action."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a carer has called before, I should still start fresh on each case, because prior helpful behaviour does not replace the need to verify identity and authority for the current request."}]}
